title: RentGuard Renters Policy Endorsement Rules — Relocation and Midterm Coverage Changes
content:
## Endorsement rules

**E-1 Status.** Midterm changes to a RentGuard Renters Policy are made only while the policy is bound, in force or pending nonrenewal, as shown on the policy record. A relocation or coverage change is not made on a policy pending cancellation, cancelled or expired.

**E-2 Relocation.** A move to a new rental residence keeps the same policy. The new address must be in Ohio; a move out of state is handled as a cancellation at the named insured's request. The rating territory is reassigned from the first three digits of the new ZIP code by the territory table.

**E-3 Relocation effective date.** A relocation reported no later than the tier's relocation reporting period after the move-in date is re-rated from the move-in date; one reported later is re-rated from the report date.

**E-4 Moving coverage.** While moving, Coverage C applies at both the old and the new residence for the tier's moving-coverage period after the move-in date.

**E-5 Coverage changes.** Changes to Coverage C, the liability limit, the deductible and the co-insured must stay within the tier's options, take effect no earlier than the request date, and are re-rated under the annual premium rating rule. A roommate is added only with the roommate's name exactly as on the lease.

**E-6 Retired clause — no longer in force.** "Every re-rating produces a new annual premium; the prorated change is the new annual premium less the old annual premium, multiplied by the calendar days from the change effective date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent." This clause has been withdrawn and superseded by the current basis for a multi-policy discount that stops or restarts during the renters term.

**E-7 Posting.** An increase is posted as additional premium and a decrease as return premium on a pro-rata basis, each with the change reason of the change and dated the change effective date. When the prorated amount is below the tier's minimum midterm premium change, nothing is posted, but the term premium is still restated.

**E-8 Interested party.** Adding, replacing or removing the landlord or property manager listed as interested party has no premium effect.

## Relocation date — boundary cases (hypothetical; reporting period of 30 days)

| Move-in date | Reported | Re-rated from |
|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 1 July (30 days after move-in) | 1 June |
| 1 June | 2 July | 2 July |

## Points of judgement

- A request made on 10 May to lower the deductible cannot take effect on 1 May.
- A hypothetical re-rating whose prorated amount is 1.40 on a tier whose minimum midterm premium change is 2.00 posts nothing, yet the new annual premium becomes the term premium.
- Replacing the property manager listed as interested party changes no premium.

superseded_clauses: Every re-rating produces a new annual premium; the prorated change is the new annual premium minus the old annual premium, multiplied by the calendar days from the change effective date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent.
